html:
SMTO-CTR-0010 — A check found the task plan left out an exact value you gave

GUID: 38e22766-fc76-47e9-82db-a2b98f81b4e1
Slug: task-contract-literal-missing
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the plan SMTO writes from a request) found that an exact value from the request, like a number, path or quoted text, is missing from the plan. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reread your request and find its exact values: numbers, file or folder paths, web addresses, names and anything in quotes. One of these values didn't make it into the plan word for word.
  2. Put each exact value in quotation marks, then send the request again as a new message so SMTO writes a new plan. Marked values stand out as text that must be kept exactly, and a new plan is checked from scratch.
  3. Don't turn off Task Contract Integrity Guard in the composer's Options menu to get past this. Turning the guard off doesn't bring back the missing value; it only removes a different protection, against plans that add locations your request didn't include.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, or the new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat a plan that failed this check as approved to run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An offline Task Contract fidelity check could not find a protected literal from the source request in the rendered contract.

What this means

  • Offline fidelity inspection cannot find a protected source literal in the rendered contract, with numeric boundaries preventing an ID from standing in for a requested number. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Offline fidelity inspection cannot find a protected source literal in the rendered contract, with numeric boundaries preventing an ID from standing in for a requested number.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the missing literal with the original source and relevant requirement; this narrow check does not prove overall fidelity.

How to fix it

  • validate_contract's fidelity check found a protected source literal (quoted or backticked text, path, URL, IP address, UUID, file name, identifier, number or unit value) absent from the rendered contract; numbers must appear as standalone values, so an ID such as R2 does not satisfy 2. Compare the source with the contract and correct or regenerate it so the literal appears exactly; keep the Integrity Guard enabled.
  • Inspect the source and contract, then use supported correction for the omitted exact requirement.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended literal remains explicitly represented when the diagnostic is rerun.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the integrity guard as a default fix.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
